findings.source_quote: καὶ εἰδότα πότε ἕκαστον ἐξ αὐτομάτου θεραπεύεται
findings.english_quote: and know when each person will recover spontaneously
findings.issue: The draft shifts the focus to a person’s recovery. In this finite clause, the neuter ἕκαστον naturally resumes the earlier ἕκαστον πάθος and the ailments described as humanly curable. Recovery from an individual ailment is not necessarily recovery of the person altogether. The notes neither explain this patient-focused paraphrase nor compare the more source-transparent ailment reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Prefer “and know when each ailment is cured spontaneously.” If retaining a patient-focused rendering, document its contextual and grammatical basis and preserve the alternative “each ailment.” This is a translation/referent question, not evidence that the verified print should be corrected.

findings.source_quote: οἱ μέντοι γε μετὰ εὐχὴν διαφωνήσαντες τὰς ἀποτυχίας ἀναθεῖναι οὐ δύνανται
findings.english_quote: Those, however, for whom matters turned out otherwise after prayer cannot dedicate their failures.
findings.issue: The broad outcome wording can function as a euphemistic rendering, but the note discusses only unsuccessful outcomes and omits the materially important sense “those who died.” The immediately following reference to relatives of the dead strongly supports that interpretation and explains why these people cannot dedicate records of their failures.
findings.suggested_revision: Either adopt “Those who died after prayer, however, cannot dedicate their failures,” with the broader failure sense preserved in a note, or retain the draft’s euphemistic wording and explicitly explain the death interpretation and its support in τῶν τεθνεώτων. The existence of these alternatives does not itself block publication.

findings.source_quote: πλὴν εἰ οἱ συγγενεῖς τῶν τεθνεώτων ἢ ἐξ αὐτῶν τινὲς συνεζήτησαν τὰς ἀποτυχίας, πλείονας ἂν εὑρήκειτε τὰς ἀποτυχίας τῶν ἐπιτευγμάτων
findings.english_quote: Yet if the relatives of the dead, or some of those people themselves, were to compile the failures, you would find the failures more numerous than the successes.
findings.issue: The draft presents a prospective hypothetical investigation. The supplied aorist indicative συνεζήτησαν and pluperfect εὑρήκειτε with ἄν instead frame a past unreal condition and its past result. The note on “compile” does not address this temporal change.
findings.suggested_revision: Render the condition retrospectively, for example: “Yet if the relatives of the dead, or some of those people themselves, had jointly investigated the failures, you would have found the failures more numerous than the successes.” Keep the unresolved referent of ἐξ αὐτῶν open rather than identifying it without evidence.

findings.english_quote: and confirm these claims with oaths
findings.issue: The feminine ταύτας points back to θεραπείας, the healings. “These claims” broadens the object to include the preceding oracle claims as well, without explaining or establishing that broader reference.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “and affirm these healings with oaths,” or another rendering that explicitly retains the healings as the object of βεβαιοῦνται.

findings.english_quote: so that it might ὑνερπολῇ and deliver oracles
findings.issue: The surviving printed verb ὑνερπολῇ remains untranslated, and the supplied documentation establishes no defensible English meaning for it. The note honestly identifies this limitation, but disclosure does not supply the missing meaning. This is not a printed lacuna, and retaining the Greek word does not complete English translation coverage. The print is already image-verified; the unresolved block concerns meaning, not suspected OCR.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide lexical or grammatical evidence establishing a defensible meaning for the exact supplied reading ὑνερπολῇ. Any correction such as the proposed ὑπερπολῇ must remain explicitly distinguished from the selected edition and supported separately; its conjectured meaning cannot silently replace the printed verb. Until a supported rendering is available, retain the disclosure and the blocked status.

findings.source_quote: ἅτινα λαβόντες πεῖραν τῶν κακῶν τοῦ λοιποῦ καταλείψετε
findings.english_quote: once you have received them, you will thereafter leave behind your experience of evils.
findings.issue: The main rendering has a defensible attachment: ἅτινα is the object of λαβόντες, and πεῖραν τῶν κακῶν is the object of καταλείψετε. However, the note does not preserve the material alternative that joins the familiar expression λαβόντες πεῖραν τῶν κακῶν, “having experienced evils,” and makes ἅτινα the object of καταλείψετε. That alternative would say that the good things are subsequently left behind. Both attachments retain the printed cases, so the note’s statement that the chosen reading avoids changing case relationships does not distinguish them.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the defensible main rendering if desired, but expand the note to give both attachments and explain that the preceding promise of good things and following thanksgiving favor the chosen reading, whereas the alternative follows the adjacent λαβόντες πεῖραν expression but produces a contextually difficult claim. Do not label the confirmed wording corrupt merely because the alternative is difficult.

findings.source_quote: οὐ πολύ, ἀλλὰ τὸ πᾶν κρείττονες
findings.english_quote: not merely a little but altogether superior
findings.issue: πολύ means “much,” not “a little.” The draft changes the degree placed under negation, and its note incorrectly says that the Greek denies a small degree of superiority. The supplied contrast is literally “not much, but the whole/altogether”; its compressed rhetorical force needs explanation rather than substitution of “little.”
findings.suggested_revision: Use a source-transparent contrast such as “superior to you not merely by much, but altogether,” with a note quoting the literal “not much, but altogether” and explaining the contextual reading as an escalation beyond a difference of degree. Preserve “in every respect” as an alternative for τὸ πᾶν where appropriate. Remove the claim that πολύ denotes a small degree; no correction of the verified Greek is warranted.
